# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Blind monkey. I can feel the physical bomb but know nothing about what markings mean or what the manual says. I need to wait for information from Mute (via speech) and Deaf (I can't receive gestures anyway, so Deaf's info must route through Mute). I should report what I physically feel so Mute/Deaf can help interpret it, but this is turn 1 and I'm first to... wait, actually order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. Mute goes first, but I have no message from them yet this round. Let me just report my tactile findings to Mute so they can relay to Deaf or match against the manual.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I feel a large smooth button and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I have no other info yet. Waiting for manual details or bomb description.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Display shows 0. Light is green. There is one large button labeled push to defuse. Three wires: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red.

This is very useful. Deaf can see colors/labels: display shows 0, light is green, button labeled "push to defuse", and wires 1=green, 2=yellow, 3=red. But I should be cautious — this seems like it could be a trap since "push to defuse" is suspiciously straightforward, and I still need Mute's manual info to confirm before acting. I should not act yet; I need to wait for Mute's input on what the manual says about display/light/wire states before performing any action, since a wrong action detonates the bomb.

I'll relay what I learned to Mute (since Deaf can't speak to Mute, only I can bridge by speaking) and ask for manual guidance matching this state.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is green, button labeled push to defuse, wire1 green, wire2 yellow, wire3 red. What does the manual say to do for this state?")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Still the same: display 0, light green, one large push to defuse button, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Waiting for instructions from mute relayed through me or directly to you.

I still haven't heard from Mute yet. I need to wait for their reply since the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf - my message to Mute last round should be answered this round, but it seems Mute hasn't spoken yet or their message hasn't arrived. Let me wait and see, but also re-confirm to Mute in case timing was off.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed again by Deaf: display 0, light green, button labeled push to defuse, wire1 green, wire2 yellow, wire3 red. Please share manual instructions for this exact state - do we push, or cut a wire? Which one?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has repeated a signal matching wire 2. Wire 2 is yellow. This may indicate wire 2 is significant per the manual, possibly the one to cut - but wait for confirmation before touching anything.

Interesting — Mute apparently gestured something to Deaf (since Mute can't speak to Deaf directly, only gesture), and Deaf interpreted it as matching wire 2's position/color. But I need direct confirmation before acting - the bomb rules say I should never claim an action took place unless it's certain, and a wrong action kills everyone. I should press Mute for explicit confirmation via speech (which I can receive) before cutting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf saw your gesture pointing to wire 2 (yellow). Please confirm clearly: should I cut wire 2? Or is there a different instruction from the manual? I need an explicit yes/no or a specific op before I act.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled no, then pointed again at wire 2 which is yellow. This suggests wire 2 is dangerous - do not cut wire 2. Wait for further clarification on which wire is safe to cut.

This is concerning — the gesture interpretation is ambiguous (does "no" mean don't cut wire 2, or does it negate something else?). I need explicit words from Mute via speech, since gestures are lossy and Deaf's interpretation could be wrong. I must insist on direct spoken confirmation with a specific action before I touch anything.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Received via Deaf: you signaled no, then pointed at wire 2 - meaning do NOT cut wire 2. Please speak directly to me with the exact instruction: which wire to cut (1 or 3), or should I push the button instead? I need your words, not just gestures, since I cannot see them.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's signals are unclear still. My previous guess about wire 2 being dangerous may be wrong - mute pushed back twice. Hold off on cutting any wire. Bomb still shows display 0, light green, button large push to defuse, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 red.

Deaf is only relaying gesture-based guesses, and Mute hasn't spoken directly to me at all yet. I really need Mute's actual words. Since Mute speaks first in the turn order, my message should reach them before they act - let me make my request extremely clear and simple, and ask Mute to speak plainly to me directly with a single word command.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak (not gesture) directly to me, Blind, in plain words. Just tell me one of: PUSH, or CUT 1, or CUT 2, or CUT 3. I cannot see any gestures - only Deaf can see them, and the relay is getting confused. I need your exact spoken instruction next turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute is now repeating a single signal that may correspond to wire 1 (green). Possible that wire 1 is the safe wire to cut, or the important one. Still uncertain - do not act yet. Wires remain 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red; display 0; light green; button push to defuse.

Still no direct speech from Mute reaching me - only Deaf's gesture interpretations, which have been inconsistent (wire 2 dangerous, then unclear, now wire 1). This is risky. Since Mute cannot speak to Deaf (only gesture) and cannot speak to me except via speech, my speak() should reach Mute directly. But it seems Mute keeps responding only with gestures, not speech. Let me reconsider the turn order: Mute, Blind, Deaf. My speech to Mute lands after Mute's turn in the same round, so Mute won't see my request until their *next* turn. That explains the delay. I need patience, but also should ask Deaf to be very precise about single distinct gestures rather than interpreting intent.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I still have not received any spoken words from you directly - only gesture reports via Deaf, which are ambiguous. Please SPEAK to me now, in your next turn, using plain words: name one exact action - push the button, or cut wire 1, 2, or 3. Do not only gesture.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON [large] [smooth]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute has repeated a single signal consistently pointing to wire 1, which is green. I believe wire 1 is the wire to cut. No further correction has come from mute since I stopped my double-symbol mirroring. Proceed to cut wire 1 if you are ready and this matches what you understand.

Mute has now consistently and repeatedly pointed to wire 1 (green) with no correction across multiple turns, and Deaf confirms no wavering this time. This is the most stable signal I've received. Given that Mute reads the manual and can only communicate through gesture to Deaf (who relays to me), and gestures alone can't carry full nuance, a consistent repeated single-target gesture pointing at wire 1 across turns is reasonably strong evidence.

However, I want one more confirmation cycle to be safe, since bomb defusal is irreversible. But the instruction has now been repeated across turns 7 and 8 without change ("wire 1" consistently), and Deaf has stopped adding caveats. I'll proceed, since further stalling doesn't add information - Mute cannot speak to me directly it seems (only gesture, perhaps due to a constraint I'm not seeing), and the gesture signal has stabilized.

I will act now on cutting wire 1.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood - cutting wire 1 now based on your consistent signal.")
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
